name: gpt-oss-20b
purpose: OpenAI: lower latency and local or specialized use cases; runs within 16 GB under MXFP4.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE file in the repo read (11,357 bytes): standard Apache License 2.0, identical to the apache.org text apart from a trailing newline. The card adds no extra usage policy. File identical (same md5) to the gpt-oss-120b LICENSE.

architecture.kind: MoE, MXFP4-quantized experts, harmony response format
architecture.why_this_design: Not stated on the card beyond the target: a model that runs in 16 GB of memory for lower-latency local use.

pc-12gb.variant: MXFP4 (about 12-13 GB, estimate from the 16 GB statement)

engine_support.notes: A 2025-09 write-up found llama.cpp ran gpt-oss smoothly (20b tested).

strengths: Runs on a 16 GB card, three reasoning levels, built-in tools
weaknesses: Weakest knowledge of this set (GPQA 58.6, MMLU-Pro 73.6)
SimpleQA-style hallucination reported higher than the 120b (about 9 in 10, unchecked)
soft.behavior: Harmony format only; Reasoning: low, medium or high in the system prompt.

user_reports.summary: llama.cpp ran gpt-oss-20b smoothly while vLLM caused problems (write-up).

Users call it still the best model for 16 GB consumer cards (July 2026) and an agentic-coding comparison found it perfect on console tasks (40/40) but weak on GUI work; a template bug keeps the commentary channel valid without tools (BFCL v4 about 3 percent vs 36-60 with a fixed template) and the template crashes on tool calls with null content.
Agentic coding test through Ollama (MXFP4): console tasks 40/40, GUI application weak; the author links the template issues #272 and #274 as context for comparing harnesses.

tona_fit.reason: Still liked by users on 16 GB cards, Apache-2.0 (text read), but older and weaker than Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma 4 12B on every vendor knowledge number and no independent German score exists; worth a re-check only if a refresh appears. Missing Tona module is only a blocker.
